name: Prowler - Cloud Security Assessment (AWS/Azure/GCP)
description: Prowler is an open-source cloud security assessment tool covering AWS, Azure, and GCP. It checks for hundreds of security misconfigurations, compliance issues (CIS, NIST, PCI-DSS, HIPAA), and best practice violations. Used defensively for cloud posture assessment and offensively to find privilege escalation and data exposure.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  pip3 install prowler
  # Or: brew install prowler

=== AWS SCAN ===
  prowler aws                              # Full AWS audit
  prowler aws --severity critical high     # Critical/high only
  prowler aws --service s3 iam ec2         # Specific services
  prowler aws --compliance cis_2.0_aws     # CIS benchmark

=== AZURE SCAN ===
  prowler azure                            # Full Azure audit
  prowler azure --service defender entra   # Specific services

=== GCP SCAN ===
  prowler gcp

=== OUTPUT FORMATS ===
  prowler aws -o json         # JSON output
  prowler aws -o csv          # CSV for spreadsheets
  prowler aws -o html         # HTML report
  prowler aws --output-directory /reports

=== KEY FINDINGS TO LOOK FOR ===
- S3 buckets with public access
- IAM users with inline admin policies
- Security groups allowing 0.0.0.0/0
- Unencrypted EBS/RDS/S3
- MFA not enforced
- CloudTrail disabled
- Root account access keys
- Cross-account trust misconfigurations

examples.label: Audit specific AWS services
examples.command: prowler aws --service s3 iam ec2 lambda

recommended.note: enumerate-iam finds what creds can do; Prowler finds what is misconfigured.

defense.why_it_works: Prowler uses cloud provider APIs to systematically check hundreds of security configurations against CIS benchmarks and best practices, identifying misconfigurations that could lead to compromise.
defense.prerequisites: Cloud credentials with read access (SecurityAudit policy for AWS, Reader for Azure).
defense.impact: Identifies misconfigurations that could lead to data exposure, privilege escalation, or compliance failures.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1580] High volume of describe/list API calls across many services from a single identity.
defense.artifacts: CloudTrail/Activity Log showing systematic read-only enumeration across services.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=aws sourcetype=aws:cloudtrail eventName="Describe*" OR eventName="List*" OR eventName="Get*"
| stats dc(eventName) as unique_apis by userIdentity.arn
| where unique_apis > 50
defense.elastic_kql: cloud.provider:"aws" AND event.action:(Describe* OR List* OR Get*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
AWSCloudTrail
| where EventName startswith "Describe" or EventName startswith "List" or EventName startswith "Get"
| summarize UniqueAPIs=dcount(EventName) by UserIdentityArn, bin(TimeGenerated, 30m)
| where UniqueAPIs > 50
defense.prevention: Restrict security audit permissions; use SCPs to limit enumeration; monitor for unusual read-only API patterns.

detections.name: Cloud security enumeration sweep
detections.logic:
AWSCloudTrail
| where EventName startswith "Describe" or EventName startswith "List"
| summarize UniqueAPIs=dcount(EventName), Services=dcount(EventSource) by UserIdentityArn, bin(TimeGenerated, 15m)
| where Services > 10 and UniqueAPIs > 100
detections.false_positives: Cloud security posture management tools; legitimate audit activities
detections.tuning: Whitelist known CSPM tool identities; focus on unusual identities
